subject.title: Codex app-server: keyed turn routing, client-scoped rate limits, and resume subscription safety

question: Should maintainers sponsor this Codex app-server safety work as split, bounded PRs on current main, or defer the broader runtime refactor for now?
rationale: The issue is protected by the maintainer label and affects auth-profile isolation, shared-client routing, and session subscription ownership, so automation should not choose the refactor scope or ownership boundary alone.

options.title: Split into bounded runtime safety PRs
options.body: Reimplement router, rate-limit cache, runtime handlers, and resume safety in smaller current-main PRs with focused tests for each invariant.

options.title: One coordinated refactor
options.body: Carry the full design in one larger PR, accepting heavier review and rebase risk to keep the lifecycle model unified.

options.title: Defer current-main reimplementation
options.body: Leave the current broad handlers and global cache in place until a maintainer prioritizes Codex app-server runtime ownership work.

recommendation.title: Split into bounded runtime safety PRs
recommendation.body: Reimplement router, rate-limit cache, runtime handlers, and resume safety in smaller current-main PRs with focused tests for each invariant.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the issue and the closed design PR that already scoped the intended fix.
